answer: Each epoch the system puts every active identity on a cryptographic ledge that demands solving a fresh reasoning puzzle whose answer ripple through a shared proof‑of‑work ledger. The puzzle is seeded by the current network state, so a fake must perform a full model inference each round, paying compute cost each time. An attacker therefore pays a linear compute harbor that scales with the number of Sybil identities, making large‑scale impersonation economically prohibitive.
